sentences.text: 03 /13.08.2024: I.A. No.7804 of 2024 This interlocutory application has been filed by the appellant, praying therein to suspend the sentence and release him on bail during the pendency of this appeal.
2. The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 366 and 376(3) of IPC and under Section 4(2) of POCSO Act, in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No.53 of 2023.
He has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 21 years with a fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offence under Section 4(2) of POCSO Act along with other sentences.

3. Heard, learned Senior counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4.
Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.
5. Though the victim is aged about 14 years, but in her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she herself stated that at night she left her house and forced this appellant to go with her.

So far as her deposition is concerned, she comes with another strange story, stating that she was sleeping with her mother and at night when she woke up, she found herself in train where this appellant was also present.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the statement, we are inclined to allow this Interlocutory application.

Accordingly,
upon suspending the sentence, the appellant, namely, Sunil Mahato @ Sunil Mahto is directed to be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rs.
Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Special Judge POCSO, Act, Dhanbad, in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No.53 of 2023 with a condition that the appellant shall appear and mark his attendance before the Registrar, Civil Court,
Dhanbad, once in every four months till the disposal of this appeal.

(ANANDA SEN, J.) (GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY, J.) R.S.
